description: `platformAutomerge` hands the merge of an automerging PR to GitHub's native auto-merge, which lands it the moment the Protect Main ruleset's required checks pass, instead of on Renovate's next run (about hourly). Safe because the required set builds, tests and renders previews (yschimke/renovate-config repo-policy: assemble, Unit tests and Render previews); native auto-merge waits only on required checks, so it would not be safe on a repository whose ruleset required nothing.

packageRules.description: The push relay's `engines.node` names a Cloud Functions runtime major ("24"), which is all Firebase accepts there: pinning it to an exact release (v24.22.1, #1244) would be refused at deploy. Keep it a bare major and only move it when a new major comes.

Temurin JDK pins (setup-java `java-version`) are installed on Linux, macOS and Windows runners, and Adoptium publishes a release for Windows x64 last: 21.0.13+9 reached Linux and macOS days before Windows, and #1082 proposed it while the Windows desktop job could only fail with 'No matching version found'. Look versions up for Windows x64, so a pin is only proposed once every runner can install it.

Offline Robolectric tests select API 35 with @Config. android-all-instrumented is an exact platform/provider image, not a library upgrade: replacing Android 15's jar with Android 17 removes the SDK Robolectric requests. Keep the catalog's SDK 35 pin until the test SDK and Robolectric provider change together.

Remote Compose, its Wear widget layer and Glance Wear resolve from Google Maven releases (the androidx.dev snapshot repository is gone). The three groups must move together — `remote-material3` and `glance-wear` both declare `androidx.compose.remote:remote-creation*` in their POMs, and a skewed set has produced runtime NoClassDefFoundErrors in the wear components — so group them into ONE PR. Alphas only: these artifacts have no stable line yet, and each alpha changes API, so the PR needs a real build, not an automerge.

DataStore stays below 1.3: with 1.3.0 a cold launch could hang in MainActivity.onCreate, its runBlocking read of the preferences store never returning (a thread dump from the phone benchmark showed the main thread parked there with nothing running), and every phone benchmark run from #1037 on failed on it. Lift this only with a phone benchmark run that passes on the new version.
Stay on JUnit 4; don't auto-bump to 5.x/6.x (Jupiter is a different API).

compose-ai-tools ships the preview CLI, the ee.schimke.composeai Gradle plugin (tracked via the compose-preview-plugin catalog key), and the reusable CI composite actions as a single release. Track it aggressively so CI always runs the latest renderer: group the pinned action refs and the Gradle plugin marker into ONE PR so the CLI catalog pin never skews apart from the action code ref, skip the weekly window, and automerge as soon as CI is green — the release moves several times a day and the pin is only useful if it keeps up. Regenerating the published catalog against the new renderer no longer depends on WHO merges: design-artifacts.yml has a push trigger on main covering the pins this PR touches, so a Renovate merge (app token — raises `push`) republishes on its own, and scheduled-merge.yml still dispatches design-artifacts.yml explicitly for the merges it makes itself (GITHUB_TOKEN merges raise no `push` event).

The contracts artifacts — the `*-core` data products, the `*-protocol` wire formats, `common-io` and the daemon transports — are released on their OWN 2.x line, independently of the 1.x plugin/CLI/actions release above, and are pinned here by the `composeai-contracts` catalog key. The rule above matches every `ee.schimke.composeai` coordinate, so without this one they get swept into the `compose-ai-tools` group PR, whose premise — 'these ship as a single release, move them together' — is simply false for them. Keeping them in their own PR means a contracts bump succeeds or fails on its own. #618 is why that matters: while `data-render-core` shared the plugin's version key, bumping the plugin dragged it to a 1.70.0 that was never published, and the resulting `Could not find ee.schimke.composeai:data-render-core:1.70.0` failed five checks at once and held the whole toolchain at 1.47.0 for weeks. #625 split the catalog key; this splits the Renovate group, so the two lines cannot be bundled back together by a matcher that predates the distinction.
